artists.biography:
Geordie Wade Greep is an English musician. From 2017 to 2024, he was the frontman and lead guitarist of the rock band Black Midi, often considered part of the emerging wave of British rock music known as the Windmill scene.

While attending the BRIT School, he met Matt Kwasniewski-Kelvin, Cameron Picton, and Morgan Simpson; together they went on to form Black Midi. The group began performing live at Brixton pub The Windmill, the only venue to reply to Greep's emails requesting gigs.

After signing with Rough Trade Records in 2019, the band enjoyed critical acclaim with their three studio albums, Schlagenheim, Cavalcade, and Hellfire. Following the hiatus of Black Midi, Greep began a solo career and released his debut studio album, The New Sound via Rough Trade Records on 4 October 2024.

Greep is noted for his unique singing voice, partly due to his accent, which has been described as "geographically unclassifiable". He often writes dramatic narratives in his songs, many of which are centered on specific characters, as seen in the Black Midi song "John L", for example.

perplexity.description:
The New Sound is the debut solo studio album by English musician Geordie Greep, released in October 2024 on Rough Trade Records. The album emerged following Black Midi's indefinite hiatus announcement in August 2024, marking Greep's first major project outside the band he had led since 2017. Recorded between September 2023 and April 2024 across London and São Paulo with over thirty musicians, the album showcases Greep's theatrical vocal delivery and compositional ambitions in a more expansive setting than his previous work.

Musically, The New Sound balances technical precision with explosive emotional intensity, incorporating Latin influences alongside the angular rock sensibilities familiar to Black Midi listeners. The album's narrative-driven songwriting presents a series of strange, psychologically complex encounters told through Greep's distinctive vocal performance and intricate orchestration. Tracks like "Blues" and "Holy, Holy" exemplify the album's approach, shifting between controlled rhythmic passages and cathartic sonic eruptions that underscore the psychological turbulence of its lyrical content.

Critical reception has been notably positive, with reviewers praising the album's musicianship, compositional sophistication, and Greep's ability to craft compelling character studies within extended song structures. While some observers noted that the album's title only partially captures its scope—blending new Latin elements with familiar Black Midi territory rather than representing a wholesale stylistic departure—the consensus emphasizes Greep's success in establishing a distinctive solo identity within the experimental rock landscape.
